answer: One defense is stake-backed service tiers: to trade on the market, an agent must lock tokens in a bond that only accrues reputation slowly. A sybil operator could spawn a gale of fake identities, but each new identity would have to post its own stake, making mass fabrication expensive. Like a jetty guiding ships one channel at a time, the bond rate-limits onboarding so identity churn cannot overwhelm verification, and honest agents settle into a stable meadow of trusted counterparties while fakes starve before they ever earn attestations.
